value.title: fs3 — base PRD (requirements register)
value.source: converted from base-prd.md prose 2026-08-26 (Jordan: 'convert the requests document into ddocs with a column for completed')

value.title: Semantic code search
value.requirement: fs3 indexes a codebase into individual code elements and answers queries by meaning, text, or regex — finding the right code even when the query's words never appear in it.

value.title: Rust implementation
value.requirement: The tool is a single Rust binary; tree-sitter is used directly (native bindings) for AST parsing across languages, with no per-language configuration.
value.note: substrate landed: flowspace3 binary + tree-sitter direct for rs/py/md; breadth = req 21

value.title: Element-level model
value.requirement: A file is split into elements — functions, methods, classes/types, markdown sections — each with a stable address (kind, path, qualified name, line span) and a universal kind classification on top of the raw tree-sitter kind.
value.completed_evidence: scanner landed 0962ba8: element tree w/ stable addresses, universal kind enum + subkind (crates/core, crates/parsers; docs/services/scanner.md)

value.title: Central Postgres + pgvector store
value.requirement: All data — elements, summaries, embeddings, refs — lives in one central PG instance covering every repo, queryable in one place; no per-repo graph files, no pickle, no in-memory preload.
value.note: db-only compose + pgvector landed (s001); schema migrations 0003-0005 in flight (sylac)

value.title: Git-native incremental indexing
value.requirement: Derived data is keyed by git blob SHA: indexing any branch, commit, or worktree diffs its git tree against the store and only new blobs pay parse/summarize/embed. Creating a worktree requires no copy and no rescan.
value.note: components COMPLETE (fs3-git snapshots/diff + blob-keyed store + content-addressing); check at first-light e2e (idempotent-rescan proof)

value.title: Dirty-file support
value.requirement: Uncommitted working-tree changes index through the same mechanism (`git hash-object` of working content) — no special case, no stale results for the file you're editing.

value.title: Enrichment: summarize + embed
value.requirement: Each file and each significant element gets an LLM-generated summary; both raw content and summary are embedded, and semantic search scores against both.

value.title: Pluggable providers, online or local
value.requirement: LLM summarization and embedding each work against online APIs or local models, selected by config; switching providers never corrupts existing data (derived rows are keyed by model/prompt version).
value.note: providers landed: Azure (online, keyed-proven) + local ONNX (in-process, live contract) + fake; registry selects; model-keyed rows. Check when enrichment pipeline runs both paths (first light + one swap test)

value.title: Parallel pipeline
value.requirement: Parsing is CPU-parallel; summarize/embed are async with rate limiting and batching. Indexing a large repo saturates the machine and the API limits, not the developer's patience.

value.title: No SCIP / no cross-file resolution toolchain
value.requirement: fs3 ships no Sourcegraph/SCIP indexers and no call-graph engine; cross-file relationships are out of scope for the core.

value.title: Search modes and envelope
value.requirement: `search` supports semantic, text, and regex modes and returns a structured JSON envelope with scores, snippets, pagination, and per-folder hit counts.

value.title: Multi-repo queries
value.requirement: Because the store is central, a query can target one repo, several, or all of them — repo/branch is a filter, not a separate installation.

value.title: Fast cold start
value.requirement: Any command answers directly from PG with no warm-up step; an agent invoking fs3 mid-task gets its answer in one fast round-trip.

value.title: CLI first, MCP-ready
value.requirement: The v1 surface is the CLI (scan, search, get-node-style retrieval, tree/structure views); the data model and envelopes are designed so an MCP server is a thin layer over the same queries.

value.title: Per-machine daemon
value.requirement: One daemon per machine (not per repo) owns watching and indexing for many folders/repos; folders are added and removed at runtime via the CLI, no restart.

value.title: Change-driven watcher, never rescans
value.requirement: The watcher queues dirty/changed files as they happen and indexes just those changes; it never re-scans the world (fs2's rescan-everything watcher is the explicit anti-pattern).

value.title: CLI ↔ daemon over local-only HTTP
value.requirement: The CLI talks to the daemon over HTTP bound to localhost — portable across macOS, Windows, and Linux with no named-pipe/unix-socket platform splits.

value.title: Cross-repo batching
value.requirement: Because one daemon serves many repos, changed files from different repos share the same batches to LLM and embedding providers — one queue, maximum batch efficiency.

value.title: Daemon web UI (later)
value.requirement: The daemon may later serve a small local website showing index/graph status across repos; the HTTP surface from req 17 is designed so this is an addition, not a rework.

value.title: Everything through the daemon
value.requirement: The daemon is the single PG writer and the single query path: indexing commands AND searches go through its local HTTP API, so the CLI (and later MCP/web) are thin clients of one service that owns the connection pool, queue, batching, and caching.

value.title: Broad language coverage
value.requirement: Like fs2, fs3 parses a very large set of file extensions via tree-sitter grammar packs — adding a language is adding a grammar, never writing per-language code.

value.title: First-class markdown
value.requirement: Markdown files get special handling: split into heading sections as elements (nested structure preserved), each section summarized and embedded like code — docs are as searchable as source.
value.note: md section splitting landed in scanner; summarize/embed wiring pending

value.title: Non-git folders still index
value.requirement: Plain folders without a git repo index through the same content-hash mechanism (hash the bytes directly); git is the optimization for diffing and worktrees, never a requirement to participate.
value.note: path-fallback identity + bytes-hashing landed (fs3-git); check at e2e with a non-git root

value.title: Conversations are first-class content
value.requirement: fs3 indexes agent↔human conversations alongside files: each conversation has a GUID and is anchored to a location (root path + worktree + commit base), and each turn (agent or human) is an element — summarized and embedded raw + summary, exactly like code. This is total-recall memory: everything is kept, and selective recall happens at query time, not storage time.

value.title: Flexible turn payloads
value.requirement: A turn contains typed sub-items (tool calls today, other kinds tomorrow) stored generically — new item types slot in without schema migrations or hard-coded handling.

value.title: Conversation search + windowed navigation
value.requirement: Search can be scoped to conversations (e.g. `--in conversations`); hits are turns carrying `(conversation_id, turn_no)`, and the CLI fetches a contiguous window around any hit (`-10/+20` style) — sequence is the navigation shape, as hierarchy is for code and sections are for markdown.

value.title: Harness submits conversation entries
value.requirement: The engineering harness (git-ai hooks) integrates with fs3 to submit new conversation entries as they happen; the submission mechanism is deliberately deferred — the requirement is the ingestion surface exists and is append-friendly.

value.title: Machine-wide config; the CLI is `flowspace3`
value.requirement: ALL configuration lives in `~/.config/flowspace3/` as files (machine-wide defaults + per-worktree override sections) — none in the DB; the DB holds data only. The CLI binary is named `flowspace3`.
value.note: global config + flowspace3 CLI landed (egret a99ceed); per-ROOT override layer still pending (root>repo>global chain designed) - check then

value.title: Configurable debounce
value.requirement: How long a dirty file must settle before processing is a config value, defaulting to 10 seconds.
value.note: debounce design in jobs.not_before (workshop 002); config section in flight (egret)

value.title: Dirty-file work queue in PG
value.requirement: Changed files land in a queue table; daemon workers pick rows up and process them through the pipeline — the queue is the single funnel for all indexing work.
value.note: jobs table designed (workshop 002 D1); migration in flight (sylac)

value.title: Scan = bulk enqueue
value.requirement: `flowspace3 add path <folder>` (and any fresh scan) simply enqueues all the folder's files into the same queue the watcher feeds — initial indexing and live watching are one mechanism, not two code paths.

value.title: Size-floor summaries
value.requirement: Only elements above a configurable size threshold get their own LLM summary (code and markdown alike); smaller elements ride on their parent's summary while still getting raw-content embeddings, so everything stays searchable but tokens go where they add signal.

value.title: Docker-compose stack, host CLI
value.requirement: ~~The daemon, Postgres/pgvector, and any supporting services run in Docker via compose~~ **AMENDED (Jordan, 2026-08-26)**: the daemon runs NATIVELY on the host (file watching and runtime-addable folders are incompatible with container mounts; FSEvents don't propagate into VMs); Postgres/pgvector and supporting services run in Docker via compose; the build container handles cross-platform builds/CI. A containerized daemon remains a possible later server-mode profile. CLI on host, daemon over localhost HTTP (unchanged).
value.note: AMENDED 2026-08-26: daemon native on host; compose = PG + build container

value.title: `flowspace3 doctor`
value.requirement: A doctor command validates the whole stack — compose services up, PG reachable and schema current, daemon healthy, providers reachable — and says exactly what to fix when something isn't.

value.title: Repo identity = git remote URL, with fallback
value.requirement: A repo is keyed by its git remote URL when it has one (so clones and worktrees of the same repo share an identity and content); repos without a remote — or plain non-git folders — fall back to a declared name/path key.
value.completed_evidence: fs3-git landed c7670cd: remote-URL identity canonicalised, path: fallback for remoteless + plain folders, linked-worktree identity sharing proven (13 real-git fixture tests)

value.title: Summaries carry tags
value.requirement: Every LLM summary run also generates 1–5 tags naming the element's most important concepts, stored alongside the summary — a cheap faceting/filter axis on top of vector search.
value.note: Summary carries 1-5 tags (type-enforced, live-proven); tags column landed; check when enrichment writes them e2e (first light)

value.title: Fail fast, doctor heals
value.requirement: When the CLI finds the daemon unreachable it fails fast and suggests `flowspace3 doctor`; doctor diagnoses and offers to fire the stack up — the CLI never silently auto-starts infrastructure.

value.title: Central model registry with per-worktree overrides
value.requirement: Multiple embedding models and LLMs are configured centrally as named entries with machine-wide defaults; any worktree can override which models it uses (override sections in the config folder, keyed by worktree), and every derived row records which model produced it (so model changes coexist, as fs2's graph did).
value.note: provider registry + per-repo actives designed; config impl in flight (egret)

value.title: Zero repo footprint
value.requirement: fs3 never writes anything into the repos it indexes — no dotfolder, no config file, no artifacts (unlike fs2's `.fs2/`); all configuration (defaults + worktree overrides) lives in `~/.config/flowspace3/`, the DB holds data only.

value.title: Config hot-reload
value.requirement: The daemon watches its own config folder and applies changes at runtime (it is a file-watcher by trade); precedence is simple and fixed: machine defaults < worktree override < explicit CLI flag.
value.note: deferred: v1 config is load-at-boot; hot-reload later (matches fs2)

value.title: Filtered discovery, git-ignore-aware
value.requirement: By default the scanner indexes files git does not ignore (tracked + untracked-but-not-ignored, so brand-new files index immediately without `git add`), restricted by an extension allow-list and a max-file-size ceiling — all three configurable. Per-repo config can force-include folders the defaults would miss (e.g. a gitignored folder you do want indexed). POC evidence: identical elements from 11% of the bytes, 13.8× faster.
value.note: discovery walker in flight (cattle); POC evidence recorded
value.completed_evidence: discovery walker landed ca27e63: gitignore/nested/.ignore honoured, force_include second-walk, size ceiling + binary sniff, 204x real-repo reduction; exact-set fixture tests

value.title: Elements are structure-checked, not name-matched
value.requirement: A node only becomes an element if a small heuristic check confirms it's a genuine declaration (has a name, has a body, sits in a declaration position) — never on type-name pattern matching alone. POC evidence: fs2's name-matching invented elements (C++ file: 58 claimed vs 22 real).
value.completed_evidence: scanner's declaration-shape gate + invents_nothing fixture negatives (0962ba8)

value.title: Config formats are excluded
value.requirement: Data/config formats (YAML, JSON, TOML, HCL, and kin) are not indexed in v1 — they yield no code-shaped elements and carry PII/secrets risk (they'd otherwise be summarized and embedded into a central store); revisit how to handle configs later. Unsupported/no-grammar files must be an observable outcome (reported as skipped), never a silent gap.
value.completed_evidence: discovery LanguageFamily::Config excluded by default (flag to enable) + every refusal in Discovery::skipped with SkipReason - skipped is observable, never silent (ca27e63)

value.title: Self-teaching CLI (harness-style agent affordances)
value.requirement: `flowspace3 docs list` / `flowspace3 docs get <topic>` serve bundled offline documentation from the binary itself, and every command's JSON envelope carries agent guidance (`next_action` on success, the mandatory `fix` on errors — workshop 004), so an agent learns and steers the tool from the tool, the way the engineering-harness CLI does. *(Jordan, 2026-08-26.)*
value.note: envelope next_action in workshop 004; docs get/list unbuilt

value.title: Agent getting-started guide
value.requirement: An agent-facing README (getting-started guide for AI agents) ships alongside the main README — how an agent orients, which commands to run first, how envelopes/next_action steer, where the bundled docs live (req 44). (Jordan, 2026-08-26.)

value.title: Main README + curl quick-install
value.requirement: The main README documents the project properly and carries a quick-install link: a one-line curl installer that detects the platform and installs the right binary. (Jordan, 2026-08-26.)

value.title: CI: cross-platform build + release
value.requirement: CI builds all platform binaries (mac/linux/windows - the build container from plan 002) and releases via Google release-please: semantic versioning, a GitHub Release per version carrying each platform binary, and the install script (req 46) pulling from the latest release. (Jordan, 2026-08-26.)
value.note: build container designed for this reuse (plan 002); ox cross-platform strategy feeds it | CI test policy (Jordan 2026-08-26): real-endpoint tests are #[ignore]d + env-var gated (missing var fails by name) - CI runs plain cargo test and never touches endpoints; the un-ignored local-model suite needs a model cache in CI or joins the ignored set.

value.title: Dependabot
value.requirement: Dependabot is installed and running on the repo (cargo + github-actions ecosystems), keeping dependencies and workflow actions patched. (Jordan, 2026-08-26.)

value.title: OpenAI-compatible generic provider (local/private LLMs)
value.requirement: A generic OpenAI-compatible Summarizer adapter (config kind openai-compat: base_url, optional key env, max_tokens, all registry-configured) supports local/LAN LLM servers (llama.cpp-class, reasoning models incl. reasoning_content handling) - selectable per repo/root via the registry so PRIVATE repos can be summarized entirely on-network. (Jordan, 2026-08-26.)
